snippet.title: 17 OCTOBRE : L'ÉTAT DÉBORDÉ PAR LES RÉVOLTES
snippet.description:
Soutenez Blast, nouveau média indépendant : https://www.blast-info.fr/soutenir

Après plusieurs semaines de mobilisation lycéenne, l'appel au 17 octobre s'est traduit par une mobilisation massive partout en France. Cortèges syndicaux, manifestations, bâtiments publics visés mais aussi de véritables mouvements insurrectionnels ont fini par submergé le dispositif policier. Mathieu Rigouste, sociologue spécialiste de la police et des mouvements sociaux analyse cette journée historique comme l'explosion d'une colère populaire, qui vise à la fois l'État et ce qu'il nomme le socio-apartheid, c'est à dire l'ordre socio-racial et de discrimination systémique.

snippet.title: CCTV shows killer student moments before he stabbed housemate 30 times
snippet.description:
A university student who lay in wait for his housemate to return home before stabbing him 30 times in a “carefully planned and cold-blooded execution” has pleaded guilty to murder.

Zack Coughlan, 23, dressed all in black and wore a mask and gloves to ambush Jamie Collins, 21, in the garden of their home in Filton, South Gloucestershire.

Bristol Crown Court heard Mr Collins was stabbed repeatedly and Coughlan left him dying in the alleyway as he cycled away on his housemate’s bike.

Coughlan had denied murder but changed his plea to guilty after a legal ruling by the trial judge on Tuesday October 20.

Mr Justice Linden ruled Coughlan’s partial defence of manslaughter by reason of loss of control could not be left to the jury to consider as part of their deliberations on the murder charge.

He told the jury: “You will have just heard that the defendant has changed his plea to the indictment to guilty.

“That means that he now admits the charge of murder.”

He added: “I would like, on behalf of us all, to thank you for the service that you have given in this case.”

Coughlan, of Cleve Road, Filton, will be sentenced on Wednesday morning.

snippet.title: Toyota owner faces $13K bill after transmission fails only 600km after warranty expiration
snippet.description:
When Dona Wilkie drove her 2021 Toyota Highlander on a recent trip to Calgary this past August to drop off her son at university, she expected a smooth ride.

Instead, the B.C. resident says she experienced aggressive gear changes and a strange noise coming from her vehicle. “As I was pressing the accelerator, it would whine. At first, quite low. It was like a humming and then it got louder as the trip went on,” said Wilkie.

Wilkie says she contacted her Toyota dealership as soon as she arrived home, only to receive shocking news.

Her Highlander, which she had purchased brand new, needed a new transmission. “I was shocked,” said Wilkie.

Making matters worse, Wilkie says she was informed by the dealership that she was 600 kilometres over the 100,000 kilometres powertrain warranty and she’d have to pay for the transmission out of pocket.

Global BC’s Consumer Matters reporter Anne Drewa reports.

For more info, please go to https://globalnews.ca/news/12108319/bc-toyota-owner-battles-automaker-bill-transmission-fails/
